pr.title: Bind MySQL command parameters as prepared statements (1.1c)
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 1.1c: MySQL command parameters are now **bound as prepared statements** instead of being written into the SQL. This finishes the SQL-injection work of 1.1:

| Database | Before #9 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| SQL Server Compact | Bound | Bound |
| PostgreSQL | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Bound (#12) |
| MySQL via MariaDB Connector/C (what the installer ships) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | **Bound (this PR)** |
| MySQL via Oracle `libmysql.dll` (fallback when `libmariadb.dll` is missing) | Inlined (injectable until #9) | Inlined, escaped single-pass (#9); removed in 1.4 |

## How it works

- **`MySQLStatement` (new):** prepares, binds and executes a command with `mysql_stmt_*`, then reads the result set.
  - Every column is fetched as a string, so the recordset reads the rows exactly as it reads a query's rows.
  - Buffers are sized from `STMT_ATTR_UPDATE_MAX_LENGTH`; a longer value is fetched again in full with `mysql_stmt_fetch_column`.
  - It is the only file that includes the MariaDB headers (for `MYSQL_BIND` and `MYSQL_FIELD`), through per-file include directories. The functions are still resolved at run time through `MySQLInterface`.
- **`SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters`** can also write MySQL's `?` placeholders: one per occurrence, so a parameter used twice is bound twice. A parameter inside a literal is still refused. `SQLStatementTester` covers both cases.
- **`MySQLConnection`:**
  - `GetSupportsCommandParameters()` is true when the MariaDB client is loaded and exports every statement function.
  - `TryExecute`, and `MySQLRecordset::TryOpen`, run a command that still has its parameters as a prepared statement.
  - Error numbers map the same way as on the query path: a lost connection is retried, and a duplicate key can be ignored by the caller.
- **Unchanged:** commands without parameters (`SET NAMES`, `USE`, `SHOW`, the internal scripts) are still sent as queries.

## Tests

`API.SqlValues`, a new regression test fixture that runs on every database:
- `TestTextValuesAreStoredAsGiven` stores and reads back text that contains quotes, backslashes, comment and statement markers, `@VALUE`, `@@ID`, `?`, `$1`, LIKE wildcards and non-ASCII characters.
- `TestLogonLooksUpTheAddressAsGiven` logs on as `o'brien@example.test`. A user name of `x' OR '1'='1` must not log on.

These are regression guards rather than reproductions: since #9, MySQL's inlined values were already escaped correctly.

## CI follow-ups in this PR

- **Headers in the CI cache:** the MariaDB Connector/C cache was pruned down to the DLL, so the build couldn't find `mysql.h`. The pruning now keeps `include` and `build64\include` and checks for them. The cache key has a `headers` marker, so caches pruned the old way aren't restored.
- **Trailing null:** `Unicode::WideToMultiByte` leaves its terminating null in the string it returns, and a bound value is sent with its length. So `+` reached MySQL as two bytes, and every domain insert failed with "Data too long". `MySQLStatement` now drops trailing nulls; the helper itself is unchanged, because its other callers use what it returns.

**Result:** CI is green on all three databases, with 1,296 tests: 1,187 passed, 0 failed, 34 inconclusive, 75 skipped (the baseline plus the two new `SqlValues` tests).

## Notes

- A command with parameters now takes a prepare and an execute (two round trips) instead of one query. Caching prepared statements per connection is possible later if it ever shows up in profiles.
- The `upgrade-mariadb` skill now lists the include directories in `hMailServer.vcxproj` as version-pinned, and checks the `mysql_stmt_*` exports.

commit.message:
Bind MySQL command parameters as prepared statements

With MariaDB Connector/C, which the installer ships, a command with parameters
now runs as a prepared statement, and its values are bound instead of written
into the SQL. That is the last database client whose values were written into
the SQL, apart from Oracle's libmysql.dll, which hMailServer still loads when
libmariadb.dll is missing and which keeps the escaped literals of
GenerateFromCommand.

- MySQLStatement prepares, binds and executes a command, and reads its result
  set with every column fetched as a string, so the recordset reads it as it
  reads a query's rows. A value longer than its buffer is fetched again in full.
  It is the only file that includes the MariaDB headers, for MYSQL_BIND and
  MYSQL_FIELD; the functions still come through MySQLInterface, which now also
  resolves the mysql_stmt_* functions.
- SQLStatement::ToPositionalParameters can write MySQL's ? placeholders: one per
  occurrence, so a parameter used twice is bound twice. Its test covers them.
- MySQLConnection::GetSupportsCommandParameters is true with the MariaDB client.
  TryExecute and MySQLRecordset::TryOpen run a command that still has parameters
  as a statement; the error number mapping is shared with the query path.
- The regression tests store values made of SQL quotes, backslashes, comment
  markers, parameter names and placeholders, and read them back, and log on as
  an account whose address contains a quote. CI runs them on SQL Server
  Compact, PostgreSQL and MySQL.
- The upgrade-mariadb skill lists the new include directories and exports.

Commands without parameters (SET NAMES, USE, SHOW, the internal scripts) are
still sent as queries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

CI: keep the MariaDB Connector/C headers in its cache

The build failed on the runner with "Cannot open include file: 'mysql.h'":
before caching the connector, the build workflow pruned its folder down to
libmariadb.dll, since nothing used the headers until MySQLStatement.cpp.

The pruning keeps include and build64\include now, and checks that mysql.h,
mariadb_stmt.h and the generated mariadb_version.h survive it - everything
mysql.h includes is in those two folders. The cache key gains a "headers"
marker, since the pruning is not in the files the key hashes and a cache pruned
the old way would otherwise still be restored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

MySQL statements: send values without the conversion's trailing null

The MySQL run failed every test in its setup: "Data too long for column
'domainplusaddressingchar'". Unicode::WideToMultiByte leaves the terminating null
of its buffer in the string it returns - GetBuffer sizes the string, and no
ReleaseBuffer trims it - which a C string never shows, so the queries and
libpq's values never noticed. A bound value is sent with its length, so "+" went
to the server as "+\0", too long for a CHAR(1), and every domain insert failed.

MySQLStatement now drops trailing nulls from the query and the string values it
converts. Unicode::WideToMultiByte itself is left as it is: its other callers
use what it returns, and some, such as the hashing, may depend on those bytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: Rewrite the README for ArzoieMail as a project of its own

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
## Summary

The README now presents ArzoieMail as a project of its own rather than as a fork's build notes. The build instructions move unchanged into `BUILDING.md`. A root `LICENSE` is added, and `.gitattributes` gets rules that actually do something.

## README

Written for people who find the project on GitHub: Windows administrators evaluating it, hMailServer users thinking of moving, and contributors.

- **Introduction:** tagline, badges, and links to [arzoie.in](https://www.arzoie.in) (download, manual, FAQ, community).
- **Where ArzoieMail comes from:** it continues hMailServer 5.7.2, explains why modernisation was needed, and who maintains it. The name origin is the wording from the website's FAQ.
- **What is different:**
  - every push is tested on all three databases, plus clean-VM test runs;
  - bound SQL parameters, and the SQL injection fixed in public;
  - hardening flags, Argon2id, and pinned, hash-checked downloads;
  - current foundations;
  - a drop-in upgrade that keeps the names existing setups use.
- **Why things were replaced:** a table of what each legacy part was, what replaces it, and why. Planned items are marked as planned.
- **Roadmap:** phases 0 to 6, including 1b (web admin), each with its status.
- **The rest:** getting started, help, security reporting (the advisory form), contributing, privacy, license and credits (Martin Knafve and the third-party licenses).

The claims were checked against the history. Before the fork, the build used the v142 toolset (VS2019) at the default C++14, the tools targeted .NET Framework 4.5, and setup's minimum was Windows Vista SP2 / Server 2008 SP2. MySQL's bound parameters are described as in progress until #17 is merged.

## BUILDING.md

The build, debug, test, code signing and release sections of the old README, unchanged. Everything that pointed at them now points at `BUILDING.md`:
- the five upgrade skills;
- `AGENTS.md`;
- the comments in `build-boost.ps1` and `build-common.ps1`;
- the manual's build how-to, which still linked `martinknafve/hmailserver`.

## LICENSE

The GNU AGPLv3 text from gnu.org, so that GitHub detects and shows the license. It is the license the installer already shows (`License.rtf`).

## .gitattributes

The old file was the Visual Studio template with every rule commented out except `* text=auto`. It keeps that rule and adds:

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| `*.bat`, `*.cmd`: `eol=crlf` | `cmd.exe` misparses labels and `GOTO` in batch files with LF endings |
| `*.ps1`, `*.sln`, `*.vcxproj`, `*.csproj`, `*.props`, `*.targets`, `*.iss`, `*.rc`, `*.reg`: `eol=crlf` | Windows-only formats, checked out the same way everywhere |
| `*.eml`: `eol=crlf` | SMTP lines end in CRLF, and the DKIM test messages' signatures cover the exact bytes |
| `*.sh`: `eol=lf` | For any future shell script |
| Images, certificates (PFX/P12/DER), DLL/EXE/MSI/LIB/TLB/SDF, archives: `binary` | Declared rather than left to detection |
| `Portable/Fuzz/corpus/**`: `-text` | Fuzzing inputs are test data; a carriage return in one is part of the input |
| `diff=cpp/csharp/php/markdown/...` | Hunk headers name the function a change is in |
| `linguist-vendored` for the Fat Cow icons, `linguist-documentation` for the manual | Keeps GitHub's language statistics about the project's own code |

`git add --renormalize .` changes no stored file, so existing files see no churn.

## Merge note

Both this PR and #17 edit `.claude/skills/upgrade-mariadb/SKILL.md`, so whichever is merged second needs a small rebase. I'll do that when the time comes.

repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

issue.body:
## Summary

Phase 1.4, the last step of the SQL work: the server **loads only MariaDB Connector/C** and **never writes values into the SQL**.

> Stacked on #17 (MySQL prepared statements), which this PR targets. When #17 is merged, GitHub moves this PR to `master`.

## Changes

- **`MySQLInterface`**
  - Loads `libmariadb.dll` only. The fallback to Oracle's `libmysql.dll`, which administrators used to copy into `Bin` themselves, is gone: its `MYSQL_BIND` layout differs from the MariaDB headers `MySQLStatement` is compiled against.
  - `Load` now fails if the library lacks any function the server uses, and the error names the missing export, instead of the server failing on first use.
  - `IsMariaDB()` and `SupportsPreparedStatements()` are removed.
- **`MySQLConnection`**: always binds parameters, and applies its MariaDB TLS options unconditionally.
- **`SQLStatement::GenerateFromCommand`** is removed with its tests.
  - `DALConnection::Execute` and `DALRecordset::Open` now refuse a command with parameters on a client that cannot bind them; they never write the values into the SQL. No current client reaches that path: SQL Server via ADO, SQL CE, PostgreSQL and MySQL all bind.
  - The positional tests keep the one case the removed tests covered that still matters: names match as whole tokens (`@ID` never matches the start of `@IDX`), and `@@IDENTITY` and a lone `@` are left unchanged.
- **Docs**: the upgrade notes say a `libmysql.dll` left in `Bin` is no longer used and can be deleted. Setup leaves it alone, since hMailServer never installed it.

## Tests

No new regression test. The refuse path can't be reached with any client the server has, and the bound path is covered by `API.SqlValues` and the MySQL CI run from #17. The `SQLStatementTester` positional cases run through `Utilities.RunTestSuite`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Three places still build SQL from `SQLStatement::Escape` instead of parameters:
- `PersistentSecurityRange.cpp:244` (a `WHERE` on the range name);
- `PersistentIMAPFolder.cpp:230`;
- `PersistentRuleAction.cpp:143`.

The escaping there is correct, but moving them to parameters would let `Escape` go as well. I suggest a small separate PR.

issue.title: Send client credentials as UTF-8

repository.name: ArzoieMail
repository.description: ArzoieMail is a free, open-source email server for Windows, forked from hMailServer. It supports SMTP, IMAP and POP3, plus anti-spam, anti-virus, DKIM, SSL/TLS, backups, scripting and a COM API. Named after my daughter Arzoie and maintained in Delhi, India.

issue.body:
## Summary

When the server logs on to another server as a client, it now sends its credentials as **UTF-8**. Until now they went in the Windows system code page, so a password containing `ä`, `✓` or a CJK character didn't work on the other server. The #21 route tests found this.

## Where it applied

| Client | Credentials | Before |
|---|---|---|
| SMTP, to the server a route relays through | AUTH LOGIN user name and password | `StringParser::Base64Encode` converted the text to the code page before base64-encoding it |
| POP3, to an external account's server | `USER` and `PASS` | `EnqueueWrite` converted the text to the code page |

So `ä` arrived as one byte that isn't valid UTF-8, and a character outside the code page (`✓`, CJK) was dropped entirely.

## Changes

- **`Unicode::ToUTF8`**: a string's exact UTF-8 bytes, without the stray terminating null that `WideToMultiByte` leaves in its output (seen in #17).
- **`SMTPClientConnection`** base64-encodes the UTF-8 of the AUTH LOGIN user name and password.
- **`POP3ClientConnection`** sends `USER` and `PASS` through a new `EnqueueWriteUtf8_`. The log still masks the password as `***`.

`StringParser::Base64Encode` is unchanged, because its other callers, such as the SMTP server's own `Username:`/`Password:` prompts, only encode ASCII.

## Tests

`Security.ClientCredentialsEncoding` uses a user name and password containing `ü`/`ä`, `✓` and `漢`:

- **`TestRouteAuthenticatesInUtf8`**: the simulated SMTP server receives exactly that user name and password. `SmtpServerSimulator` now also records the AUTH LOGIN user name.
- **`TestExternalAccountLogsOnInUtf8`**: `Pop3ServerSimulator` now records `USER` and `PASS`.
  - The simulator reads plain connections as ASCII, so each byte above 127 shows up as `?`.
  - The test therefore expects one `?` per UTF-8 byte: two for `ü`, three for `✓`.
  - The old code-page encoding would give one `?` or none, so the test tells the two apart.
